summary: lil-bench shows the real KV capacity of hybrid models such as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
compatibility: Rerun lil-bench in the new image; results uploaded earlier keep the KV capacity they showed.
details: lil-bench computed the KV capacity as blocks × block size. Hybrid models share one block pool across their layer groups, so that overstated it many times over: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP2 showed 86M KV tokens where the server holds 4.8M, and TP4 100M instead of 6.5M.

It now uses vLLM's own KV capacity (kv_cache_size_tokens), which already counts every DCP rank. The number is shown at the start of the run and decides which decode cells are skipped for capacity (lil-bench 1.3.2, llm-inference-bench v0.7.5). Reported by auldria.
